existing.description: The Swedish Institute, a Swedish government agency, awards fully funded scholarships for master's studies in Sweden to global professionals from 34 eligible countries. The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals covers full tuition fees, a monthly living-expense allowance of SEK 12,000 and a one-time travel grant, and runs once a year for master's studies starting in the autumn semester. The Swedish Institute also runs the Pioneering Women in STEM scholarship, awarded through the same single application. The 2026/2027 call closed on 25 February 2026 and recipients were announced on 23 April 2026; the next call is expected to be published on si.se in mid-November 2026.
eligibility: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Egypt, Ethiopia, Georgia, Guatemala, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Liberia, Malaysia, Mexico, Moldova, Morocco, Nigeria, Peru, Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Zambia
Liability to pay tuition fees at University Admissions
Admitted or conditionally admitted to an eligible programme on the admissions results day (26 March 2026 for the 2026/2027 cycle)

At least 3,000 hours of proven work experience prior to February 2026 for applicants from Bangladesh, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Egypt, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Liberia, Malaysia, Mexico, Morocco, Nigeria, Peru, Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Vietnam and Zambia
No minimum hours for applicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine, but more experience is prioritised
Not currently enrolled in or holding a degree from a Swedish university or university college
Not having resided in Sweden for cumulatively two years or more before the scholarship period (starting August 2026)
existing.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's degree, 3000 hours work experience, leadership qualities, apply to Swedish university simultaneously
requirements: Citizen of one of the 34 eligible countries (residency in that country not required)
Liability to pay tuition fees to Swedish universities
Admitted or conditionally admitted to an SI-eligible master's programme on the University Admissions results day
Demonstrated work experience, certified on SI's template
Demonstrated leadership experience from a current or previous employer, or civil society engagement
Not a previous holder of a Swedish Institute scholarship for studies in Sweden
Not a Swedish or EU/EEA citizen, and no Swedish permanent residence or work/family-based permit
application_method: Apply for an eligible master's programme at University Admissions (universityadmissions.se) and pay the application fee
Save the eight-digit University Admissions application number
Submit one SI scholarship application at apply-scholarships.si.se listing up to four eligible programmes
Keep the admissions offer unchanged; reserves and late admissions are not eligible
existing.selection_notes: SI scores applications against the aim of the programme and the government strategy it reports to, prioritises work and leadership experience relevant to the chosen field, aims for gender balance and country spread, and states it has no quotas for specific countries, fields of study or universities.
existing.notes: The scholarship does not include insurance, does not provide additional grants for family members, does not cover the University Admissions application fee, does not allow changes to the study programme and does not allow extensions or changes to the scholarship period.
existing.duration: One- or two-year full-time master's programme
existing.application_period: Annual cycle. For academic year 2026/2027: university applications 16 October 2025 - 15 January 2026, SI scholarship portal 9-25 February 2026, results 23 April 2026.
existing.program_type: Government scholarship (Swedish Institute public agency), master's level

existing.description: A one-month funded research stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala for Africa-focused researchers and students already based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland. The scholarship covers return travel at the least expensive fare, free centrally located accommodation in Uppsala, a desk and computer in a shared office at the Institute, and a subsistence allowance of SEK 450 per day. It is a short-term research stay award, not a degree programme.
eligibility: You must be pursuing Africa-oriented studies/research within the fields of social sciences or humanities
You can be a master student, PhD candidate, postdoctoral or mid-career researcher

You may apply regardless of citizenship, but you must be affiliated to and based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland (both when you apply and when you take up the scholarship)
The scholarship is awarded for a one-month stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala
existing.eligibility_summary: Africa-oriented studies or research in the social sciences or humanities, with a current affiliation to a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland, held both at the time of application and when the scholarship is taken up.
benefits: Access to the Nordic Africa Institute's library collections on contemporary Africa (books, periodicals, newspapers, and government publications)
Support to connect to existing work at the Institute through NAI research hosts
Access to a workspace in a shared office at the Institute for the one-month stay
coverage: Travelling expenses for the least expensive fare from residential address (in Sweden, Finland, Denmark and Iceland) to Uppsala and return
Free accommodation centrally located in Uppsala
A subsistence allowance of SEK 450 per day
A desk and computer in a shared office at the Institute for the one-month stay
Access to the Institute's library collections on contemporary Africa (books, periodicals, newspapers, and government publications)
Connection to existing work at the Institute through NAI research hosts
requirements: The application and appendices must be in English
Incomplete applications will not be considered
The application must be uploaded with all four listed documents
documents: Up-to-date CV, including list of publications (if any)

Outline of research project, 3-5 pages: objective of the research project (the research topic should be clearly identified and contextualized within its academic discipline); method and time frame (how the research project will be accomplished, the research method, data gathering techniques and time frame); theoretical explication (a brief indication of the theoretical basis of the research project)
Work plan, 1 page: specific for the time spent at the Institute, clarifying what part of the research project the applicant will work on during the stay
Reference: a signed letter of support from the applicant's supervisor or head of department, which confirms current affiliation and field of research
existing.english_requirement: The application and all appendices must be in English.
application_method: Open the Nordic Scholarship Programme 2027 application link on the Nordic Africa Institute opportunities page
Register and complete the online application
Upload the up-to-date CV including list of publications (if any)
Upload the 3-5 page outline of the research project covering objective, method and time frame, and theoretical explication
Upload the 1 page work plan specific to the stay at the Institute
Upload the signed reference letter from the supervisor or head of department confirming current affiliation and field of research
Submit before the closing date of 11 October 2026
Wait for the outcome, which is communicated as soon as the selection process is finalized and by the end of November 2026 at the latest
existing.selection_notes: Applications are primarily evaluated based on the outline of the research project. The Institute states that it reads proposals carefully and that it is important to learn about the applicant's research in their own words and framing, and that using AI to develop the text may place an applicant at a disadvantage in the assessment process. Scholarships are awarded once per year.
existing.best_fit: Master's students, PhD candidates, postdoctoral and mid-career researchers based in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland whose work is Africa-oriented and located in the social sciences or humanities
existing.notes: The scholarship does not include health care insurance or other insurances. Persons currently or previously employed by or otherwise professionally affiliated with the Nordic Africa Institute are not eligible for scholarships. In the extraordinary event that the scholarship programme does not receive full funding or cannot for other unforeseen reasons be implemented in 2027, applicants will be informed accordingly. Successful candidates who have been awarded but cannot take up the stay are not covered by any published replacement policy. Applications are submitted once per annual round.
existing.duration: One-month stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala
existing.application_period: Open now for scholarships in 2027, closing 11 October 2026; applicants informed of the outcome by the end of November 2026 at the latest
